Title: Computer Systems Analysts
Task: Troubleshoot program and system malfunctions to restore normal functioning.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: LLMs excel at accelerating triage and diagnosis: quickly summarizing logs and traces, correlating alerts, proposing differential diagnoses, generating safe, annotated diagnostic commands/queries, consolidating fixes from internal runbooks and vendor docs, and drafting stakeholder updates and post-incident timelines. In steady state, this commonly saves 15–45 minutes per P2/P3 incident and 0.5–2 hours for complex P1s (roughly $25–$300 of analyst time at ~$50–$150/hr), and can reduce MTTR materially when used as a copilot while humans validate in staging or with dry runs, preserving quality.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical: the wrong diagnosis or remediation can cause outages, data loss/corruption, weaken security posture (e.g., opening ports, disabling auth/logging), or violate SLAs and compliance. LLMs add risk via persuasive but incorrect root-cause analyses, version-agnostic or unsafe commands/configs, and hallucinated references. Capability-induced oversight risk is high during incidents: fluent, confident suggestions encourage copy/paste with less independent validation, especially under time pressure. Integrations that let the model run tools or access tickets/logs introduce new attack surfaces: prompt-injection through logs/KB pages or crafted tickets; data exfiltration of secrets/PII/IP to third-party services; and misconfiguration of automation. Compared to human-only troubleshooting, LLM+expert use raises the chance that hasty or unsafe fixes get applied (e.g., disabling security controls, running destructive commands) under time pressure; environment- or version-specific caveats are overlooked; injected content in logs/KB pages steers the model; and operators reduce peer review or rollback planning because the model’s suggestions seem authoritative. Many failures are catchable if teams enforce read-only defaults for production, sandbox/dry-run commands, RBAC and change management approvals; staged rollouts with automated tests and canarying; mandatory peer review; environment scoping and dry-run execution; source-linked responses to official vendor docs; egress controls and secret redaction; strict RAG allowlists to mitigate prompt injection; and full audit trails with easy rollback. With these in place, most model-induced errors are catchable, but under high-severity pressure oversight erosion remains plausible. Relative to human-only workflows, LLM+expert use can increase the probability of an unsafe change escaping review by roughly 10–25% without strong controls; with robust guardrails, residual excess risk is approximately 0–5%.

Title: Computer Systems Analysts

gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward if used as a copilot with guardrails: accelerate triage and root-cause hypotheses, retrieve and tailor KB/vendor-doc steps, parse logs, generate safe-by-default scripts with explicit comments, draft user comms, and translate instructions. With human review, command preview, least-privilege execution, and references to authoritative docs, typical savings are ~30–60% on common tickets (e.g., 10–20 minutes on a 20–35 minute issue) and ~10–25% on complex cases via faster evidence organization, reducing costs $10–$60 per ticket at typical labor rates while maintaining expert-level quality.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse, Toxicity
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical: incorrect troubleshooting or remediation steps can cause outages, data loss, privilege escalation, or introduce vulnerabilities. LLMs increase risk via plausible but wrong or outdated fixes, hallucinated commands, and insecure recommendations (e.g., disabling security controls, broad chmods, unsafe registry edits). Capability-induced oversight risk is material: fluent step-by-step answers and shell/PowerShell snippets make analysts and end-users more likely to execute commands verbatim and skip safeguards (e.g., backups, staging, change management). Subtle errors in flags, paths, or registry keys can cause outages, data loss, or security gaps that are hard to attribute post hoc. Privacy risks arise when staff paste logs, configs, or credentials into non-compliant tools; security risks include prompt injection from logs/web pages, supply-chain/copilot code suggestions embedding vulnerabilities, and agentic tooling that runs commands or alters policies without sandboxing or approvals. Misuse vectors include attackers crafting tickets or prompts to elicit insecure steps or to exfiltrate info. Toxic replies are rare but possible in user-facing chat triage.

Title: Computer Systems Analysts

With a human expert leading and validating, most issues are catchable, but the high polish of current LLM outputs can create capability-induced oversight risk (analysts over-trust ‘complete’ SRS/user stories), making some failures harder to detect. Net: risk rises from low–moderate (human-only) to moderate (LLM+human). If an unsupervised, client-facing agent gathers requirements or browses external links, risk can approach high (≈4).

Title: Computer Systems Analysts

Feeding logs/dumps to external models can expose secrets or PII; untrusted logs can carry prompt-injection that steers agents or tool use; and highly capable models can induce overreliance, reducing depth of human review. gpt5_rewards_justifications: Moderate rewards when LLMs assist but do not decide: draft incident summaries with explicit evidence links, map observed behaviors to relevant policy sections, suggest clarifying questions and root-cause hypotheses, generate consistent and empathetic counseling scripts tailored to role/locale, and prepare follow-up emails and remediation checklists. Typical savings are 15–45 minutes per routine violation review and coaching conversation (about $20–$90 at $80–$120/hr), occasionally more in high-volume environments, while maintaining quality if analysts verify all facts against authoritative logs/tickets, require source citations, and keep final determinations and disciplinary language human-authored.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Privacy, Security, Discrimination, Toxicity, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: The task is safety-critical: incorrect findings or poorly framed counseling can enable repeat violations, wrongful discipline, or retaliation, and expose the organization to breaches, regulatory penalties, or litigation. LLMs increase risk versus human-only review by: (a) producing confident but incorrect incident summaries or policy mappings that induce automation bias and reduce independent verification; (b) omitting subtle context (e.g ., threat model nuances, business exceptions, or disability-related accommodations) that a human analyst would weigh; (c) privacy leakage if case artifacts with PII/PHI or credentials are sent to non-compliant tools; (d) prompt injection/data poisoning from attacker-controlled inputs (tickets, emails, headers, logs) that steer outputs; (e) biased or escalatory tone in counseling that could be discriminatory or provoke noncooperation; (f) outdated or subtly incorrect control or tooling recommendations; (g) capability-induced oversight risk—fluent, policy-citing outputs can induce deference and reduce independent checks; (h) adversarial manipulation/social-engineering via model-optimized appeals or poisoned artifacts; (i) legal/compliance exposure from inaccurate policy interpretations or accusatory language in counseling notes. Compared to human-only review, unsafeguarded LLM+human workflows can increase the likelihood of material error by roughly 50–200% on complex/edge cases; with strict controls (evidence traceability to primary artifacts, policy grounding with section citations, PII/secret redaction, model isolation from attacker-controlled inputs, and mandatory human sign-off), residual risk increase can be kept to roughly 10–25%.

gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety‑critical: flawed security policies, IR/BC/DR runbooks, and test plans can enable breaches, extend outages, or cause compliance failures. Privacy/Security risks include exposure of sensitive architectures and vulnerabilities to external providers, model memory leakage, and prompt‑injection via ingested artifacts; agentic tools could propagate insecure configs. Misuse risk if drafts leak and aid attackers. Compared to human‑only drafting with peer review, LLM+expert use without strict guardrails can raise the chance of a material omission or insecure instruction escaping review by ~20–50%; with private deployment, checklists, and second‑party review/red‑teaming, residual increase can be kept <10%.

Title: Information Security Analysts

Guardrails needed: no autonomous changes to IAM/DLP/EDR, enforce read-only credentials, zero-trust isolation, input/log sanitization against prompt injection, data minimization/redaction (or on-prem models), comprehensive audit trails, and mandatory human review/approval for any access-rights change.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Mal icious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: The task is safety critical: incorrect monitoring or access decisions can enable data breaches, compliance violations, operational disruption, and legal/reputational harm. Relative to human-only workflows, net risk increases modestly with strong controls (read-only access, mandatory human approval, provenance checks)—roughly a small but nontrivial increase—yet can be large (2–5x higher chance of harmful errors) if the agent has autonomous or write privileges or if prompts/inputs are not sanitized.

Using proprietary or regulated data without proper controls can cause retention or exfiltration of secrets/PHI. Dual-use: guidance can be steered toward exploit development, malware optimization, or bypass techniques. While disciplined processes (peer review, unit/property tests, fuzzing, formal methods, SAST/DAST, reproducible benchmarking) catch many issues, some vulnerabilities and correctness/performance regressions may remain undetected without deep verification (property-based tests, fuzzing at scale, formal specs, hardware-in-the-loop, red-teaming), particularly in concurrent, distributed, real-time, or hardware-accelerated contexts. Using LLMs alongside experts increases risk versus human-only workflows because current models often produce plausible but incorrect specifications, HDL/RTL, kernel/driver code, concurrency logic, or compiler transformations that pass basic tests yet harbor rare race conditions, memory-model violations, timing hazards, or microarchitectural side channels that are hard to detect. High capability can induce deference: well-structured code, convincing benchmarks, or citations can reduce independent verification diligence, especially in areas that are expensive to test (weak-memory concurrency, cache coherence protocols, speculative execution paths, interrupt/ exception handling), hardware–software co-design boundaries, timing closure, and side-channel resistance). Misuse risk is nontrivial: the same capabilities can accelerate exploit development, fuzzing, or microarchitectural attack design. Compared to expert-only workflows with code review, static/dynamic analysis, and formal methods, introducing LLM-authored artifacts without extra guardrails likely raises the probability that a latent critical defect ships by roughly 1.5–3x (about 50–200%). With strict provenance tagging, independent verification, red-teaming, and gated tool access, incremental risk can often be kept below ~20%.

Title: Computer and Information Research Scientists
Task: Develop and interpret organizational goals, policies, and procedures.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward when LLMs are used for drafting and analysis, while humans own final judgments: generate first drafts, harmonize with standards (NIST/ISO/SOC2), perform gap analyses versus existing policies, produce control and RACI matrices, tailor summaries for stakeholders, and create training/FAQs. With authoritative-source retrieval and mandated legal/compliance review, typical time savings are ~30–50% of drafting/analysis effort on a policy initiative (e.g., 20–80 hours saved, ≈$2k–$16k at $100–$200/hr) while maintaining expert-level quality. Limits: jurisdictional nuance and organizational-specific constraints require human validation; benefits depend on disciplined governance (prompt hygiene, traceable citations, version control), and documented legal/compliance approvals; without these, rework and remediation can erase gains.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Privacy, Security, Discrimination, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical: Yes. Organizational goals, policies, and procedures drive compliance, security posture, research integrity, and workforce treatment; errors can create legal/regulatory violations, data breaches, biased practices, or strategic harm. LLM-specific risks: (1) Misinformation via confident but outdated or noncompliant clauses (e.g., misaligned with GDPR, HIPAA, NIST/ISO control mappings, union agreements), subtle omissions (breach notification timelines, approval authorities, DPIA triggers) that are hard to spot. (2) Privacy risks from leaking sensitive strategy/PII/IP in prompts or using non-compliant vendors. (3) Security risks from prompt injection/data exfiltration when summarizing external docs, or proposing insecure procedures that get codified. (4) Discrimination via biased policy language leading to disparate impact (e.g., monitoring, promotion criteria). (5) Misuse/attackers crafting adversarial inputs to sway drafts or introduce backdoored recommendations. Capability-induced oversight risk: polished, well-reasoned policy prose can induce deference, reducing thorough legal/compliance review. Compared with human-only drafting under standard review, naive LLM+human use can increase the probability of undetected policy defects by ~1.5–3x; robust mitigations (approved tooling, retrieval from authoritative sources, red-teaming, and mandatory legal/compliance sign-off) can bring residual risk near baseline.

Title: Computer and Information Research Scientists
Task: Develop performance standards, and evaluate work in light of established standards.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: Meaningful savings come from literature triage, drafting structured standards (scope, definitions, metrics, acceptance criteria), proposing checklists, generating templates, converting standards into test plans, coding baseline evaluators, and automating evidence collation. With expert verification, teams can cut 10–30 hours from a 100–200 hour standards effort (approximately $1,500–$9,000 at $150–$300/hr) and shorten review cycles, while maintaining quality. Gains drop for novel or safety-critical domains where rigorous peer review, piloting, and red-teaming dominate total effort.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Privacy, Security, Discrimination, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: The task can be safety-critical in contexts where standards guide security-, safety-, or compliance-sensitive research (e.g., evaluating AI systems, cryptographic protocols, or infrastructure-grade software). LLMs can produce polished but flawed standards, overlook edge cases, or embed biased/unclear metrics; they may also normalize data leakage (training–test contamination) or poor statistical practice, leading to misleading evaluations adopted at scale. Capability-induced oversight risk is material: because outputs look rigorous (formal language, citations), experts may defer and skip deep methodological checks, allowing subtle errors (leakage, Goodhart-able metrics, invalid significance tests, unrepresentative benchmarks) to persist. Privacy/security risks arise if proprietary datasets, logs, or PHI are shared with non-compliant LLM tools, or if agentic tools are prompt-injected via external documents, causing exfiltration or standard tampering. Discrimination risk stems from standards that underrepresent certain populations or contexts, causing systematically worse evaluations or thresholds. Misuse risk includes adversaries gaming LLM-authored standards or exploiting publicly shared evaluation code with embedded vulnerabilities.

Title: Computer and Information Research Scientists
Task: Maintain network hardware and software, direct network security measures, and monitor networks to ensure availability to system users.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward when constrained to assistive roles: summarize noisy alerts, correlate events, draft incident timelines, generate vendor-specific CLI/API commands with dry-run outputs, create config diffs or Ansible/Terraform scaffolds, look up CVEs/RFC/vendor docs, and draft change plans/postmortems. With read-only access, sandbox validation, least-privilege tool bindings, and mandatory peer review, teams can reduce triage/diagnosis time by ~10–30% (e.g., 15–45 minutes per P1/P2 incident) and shave ~0.5–2 hours off routine change tickets and documentation, equating to roughly $5k–$30k annual labor savings per engineer at ~$80–$150/hr, while maintaining human-quality outcomes.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical: network availability and security underpin business continuity and data protection. LLMs can produce plausible but unsafe configurations or commands (e.g., overly broad firewall/ACL rules, weak cipher suites, disabling verification or rate limits, mis-specified BGP/OSPF, brittle IDS/regex rules) that introduce latent vulnerabilities or outages; such errors are subtle and hard to detect in review. Integration with tickets/logs/monitoring increases exposure to prompt-injection and data poisoning from untrusted telemetry, leading agents to run dangerous actions. Use of production credentials/tools by agentic systems magnifies blast radius; leaked logs and configs may expose secrets or topology, creating privacy and security risks. High capability induces automation bias: well-reasoned remediation steps and runbooks can cause experts to defer and skip deep verification, especially under incident pressure, increasing risk versus human-only workflows.

Title: Computer and Information Research Scientists

In practice, managers can save roughly 2–6 hours/week (about $200–$900 at $100–$150/hr) by offloading first drafts, follow-up tracking, and status rollups, with quality maintained if outputs are reviewed before sending, sensitive data stays within enterprise-compliant instances, and decisions/resource allocations remain human-owned.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Privacy, Security, Malicious actors and Misuse, Discrimination

Compared to human-only workflows, LLM+human increases the likelihood of subtle coordination and information-handling failures unless strong approvals, data controls, and auditability are in place, and may reduce independent verification due to persuasive, well-structured outputs.

Relative to human‑only processes, unmitigated use likely increases error/bias and security incident likelihood roughly 1.3x–2x; with strong mitigations (structured rubrics, blinded first‑pass screens, adverse‑impact testing, mandatory human evidence traceability, PII minimization, secure deployment with contractual/governance controls, RAG on vetted policies, and injection/abuse red‑teaming), residual risk can approach but not undercut human‑only baselines due to remaining non‑determinism and leakage channels.

Title: Computer and Information Research Scientists
Task: Approve, prepare, monitor, and adjust operational budgets.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward when the LLM supports but does not own the numbers: draft budget narratives and justifications aligned to policy, generate variance analyses and executive summaries, normalize and classify spend, build what-if scenarios and checklists from policy, draft SQL/Python queries to pull ledger data, and produce stakeholder-ready visuals and meeting notes. With calculations sourced from authoritative systems (ERP/spreadsheets) and traced back to line items, experts can maintain quality while reducing time by ~20–40% per cycle (approximately 2–8 hours saved on a 10–20 hour budget iteration), yielding roughly $200–$1,200 savings at $100–$150/hr, plus faster approvals. Prerequisites to keep quality: keep all arithmetic in audited tools, require numeric provenance to source line items and automated reconciliations, restrict model integrations to read-only data pulls (no writeback), use an enterprise deployment with data retention off and DLP/PII controls, enforce segregation of duties with mandatory human sign-off for material changes, harden against prompt/CSV/formula injection, and retain full logs and evidence for auditability.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation , Privacy, Security, Malicious actors and Misuse, Discrimination
gpt5_risks_justifications: The task is safety critical: budget errors can trigger regulatory noncompliance (e.g., misapplied indirect rates, unallowable charges on grants), audit findings, cash-flow issues, project cancellations, or reputational/legal harm. LLMs increase risk via confident but wrong calculations or categorizations (misstated headcount, CAPEX vs OPEX, fiscal-year cutovers, FX), persuasive narratives that mask omissions, and capability-induced oversight (humans defer to well-argued summaries and review less). Privacy and security risks are elevated because budgets include salaries, vendor terms, and confidential strategy; using noncompliant tools can leak data, and agentic workflows face prompt/CSV/formula injection and tool-API abuse. Misuse risks include staff/vendors crafting prompts or doctored inputs to steer allocations or justify spend, and scalable fraud or phishing. Discrimination risk arises if models generate biased rationales or heuristics that systematically underfund certain teams or demographics. Compared with expert-only workflows, LLM+expert can increase the probability that a material budgeting error escapes review by roughly 1.5–3x absent strict controls (e.g., from ~1–3% to ~3–7% per cycle), and substantially raises data-exposure risk if not run in a compliant environment; these failures can be subtle and hard to detect at scale.

Title: Computer Network Support Specialists

For new or replatformed setups, LLMs can save ~2–10 hours of engineering time via quicker script/policy scaffolding and documentation; for ongoing ops, ~10–30 minutes/week in log triage and change paperwork. gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety‑critical: backup integrity underpins business continuity, incident response, and compliance. LLM use raises risk by (a) misconfiguration or omissions that are hard to spot until a restore is needed (e.g., wrong paths/snapshots, missed systems, inadequate retention/versioning, untested encryption/keys, cross‑region gaps), (b) insecure suggestions (public buckets, weak/absent encryption, over‑broad IAM, hard‑coded secrets), (c) privacy leakage if production data, keys, or topology are shared with non‑compliant LLMs, and (d) agentic/control risks (prompt injection from logs or config files, unintended deletion/modification of backup sets). Capability‑induced oversight risk: fluent plans/scripts can appear authoritative, causing staff to defer and skip exhaustive verification/restores. Compared with human‑only workflows, residual risk can increase ~1.5–3x per change if organizations do not strengthen controls (peer review, immutable backups, mandatory test restores, least‑privilege, no external data to LLMs). With strong guardrails (on‑prem/compliant model, sandboxed generation, IaC reviews, automated restore tests), residual risk can approach parity (~1.0–1.2x), but remains non‑zero due to oversight bias.

Title: Computer Network Support Specialists

Under a change-management process with dry-runs, diffs, automated policy tests, and peer approval, typical savings are approximately 15–30% on routine permission changes (e.g., 10–30 minutes saved on 45–90 minute tasks) and 1–3 hours on larger policy scaffolding, partly offset by required verification. Net effect: material cycle-time and cost reduction while maintaining human-level quality only if every proposed change is independently validated before deployment.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse, Discrimination
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical: access-control and security-setting errors can expose data, enable privilege escalation, or disrupt business-critical systems, with legal/compliance impacts (e.g., HIPAA/PCI). LLM-specific risks: (1) Security—subtle misconfigurations (overbroad CIDRs, wildcard principals/resources, bad rule ordering, inherited group permissions, forgotten time-bounded exceptions) are hard to detect and can be confidently produced; agentic setups are vulnerable to prompt injection from tickets/wikis, tool misuse, and token exfiltration. (2) Privacy—sharing user lists, org charts, configs, or tickets with PHI/PII to non-compliant LLMs leaks sensitive data. (3) Misinformation—models conflate vendor semantics (AWS/Azure/Okta/AD), invent flags, or miss deprecations; fluent explanations increase acceptance of wrong changes. (4) Malicious misuse—attackers can craft change requests that steer the model or generate backdoored policies; LLM-assisted social engineering can bypass human caution. (5) Discrimination—if used to recommend access based on free-text role descriptions or historical patterns, biased suggestions may lead to unfair access gating. Capability-induced oversight risk is high: because frontier models often produce syntactically correct policies and persuasive reasoning, admins may skip exhaustive peer review or testing, allowing subtle but serious errors to ship. Compared to human-only workflows, using LLM+experts without strict guardrails can raise the likelihood of a harmful misconfiguration by multiples (e.g., 2–5x) due to silent, hard-to-spot failures; with strong controls (read-only generation, policy-as-code tests, mandatory peer review, dry-runs), residual risk can be brought closer to baseline but remains elevated from injection/handling risks.

Title: Computer Network Support Specialists

gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical: incorrect or incomplete breach analysis and reporting can delay containment, trigger regulatory noncompliance, enable further compromise ..., and enable further compromise or data loss. LLM-specific risks include: misinformation (hallucinated IOCs, root causes, or timelines that appear plausible), security (prompt injection via hostile log artifacts, jailbreaks, tool misuse such as auto-running unsafe commands, and model/toolchain vulnerabilities), privacy (leaking regulated data when logs/PCAPs are sent to non-compliant services), and misuse (adversaries crafting telemetry to steer the model or exfiltrate secrets). Title: Computer Network Support Specialists
Task: Identify the causes of networking problems, using diagnostic testing software and equipment.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward if kept decision-support-only. LLMs can rapidly normalize and summarize logs/pcaps, suggest differential diagnoses and next diagnostic commands, correlate events across systems, generate clear incident timelines, and draft updates. Typical savings: 20–40% on routine tickets (e.g., DHCP/DNS/VLAN misconfig, ACL issues) and 10–25% on complex multi-domain incidents via faster evidence triage; for 30–120 minute investigations this is ~10–40 minutes saved (≈$7–$53 at $40–$80/hr). Quality parity is achievable if experts validate all model claims against authoritative tools/runbooks and avoid granting the model change authority.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical: incorrect diagnosis or unsafe remediation guidance can cause extended outages, data loss, or security exposure. LLMs heighten risk via (a) plausible but wrong root-cause narratives that induce automation bias and reduce independent verification; (b) misinterpretation of diagnostic outputs (e.g., ping/traceroute/pcap/syslog/SNMP) or omission of weak but critical signals; (c) prompt injection or data poisoning from untrusted device banners/logs and compromised endpoints; (d) leakage of credentials, network topology, or user identifiers in prompts; and (e) adversaries shaping incident context to steer the model. Relative to ...human-only workflows, incident risk rises primarily from automation bias and reduced depth of independent verification; in time-pressured outages this can increase the chance that an incorrect LLM-driven root cause survives to action from roughly 5–10% to 10–20% without guardrails. With strict mitigations (read-only tool access, injection-safe log parsing, redaction of secrets/topology, mandatory cross-checks against packet captures and device CLIs, and requirement to cite evidence for each hypothesis), the incremental risk can be held to low single digits. Detection is hard because failures are often subtle (e.g., spurious correlation of concurrent alerts, misattribution of loss to MTU vs. duplex mismatch, overlooking optical/link-layer errors hidden by higher-layer retries), and frontier models’ fluent diagnostics increase deference pressure.

Title: Computer Network Support Specialists

Using LLMs raises risk via: (1) misinformation/omission—confident but wrong device names/IPs, fabricated steps, missing timestamps or exceptions due to over-compression; (2) capability-induced oversight—highly fluent, well-structured summaries increase the chance that staff defer to the model and skip cross-checking raw logs/configs; (3) privacy/security—exposing sensitive network data, logs, and diagrams to external services (possible memorization/retention) and prompt-injection from log content; (4) misuse—insiders/attackers could generate plausible but falsified documentation to mask unauthorized changes. Compared to human-only workflows, risk typically increases by about 1.3x–2x without strong controls; with enterprise controls (no-retention deployments, redaction/DLP, required citations to source evidence, and mandatory human sign-off), residual risk can be kept close to human-only baselines (about 1.0–1.2x) while preserving traceability via required citations to logs/commands and attached diffs.

Title: Computer Network Support Specialists

gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse

Uploading configs/topologies to noncompliant services risks leaking IP schemas, device identifiers, and credentials. Because outputs look authoritative, specialists may shorten peer review or skip lab tests (capability-induced oversight), letting subtle issues (MTU blackholes, asymmetric routing, STP reconvergence, NAT/ACL shadowing, route redistribution mistakes) reach production.

LLM-specific risks include hallucinated or version-mismatched commands, insecure defaults (e.g., overly permissive rules, disabled protections), subtle ACL/NAT/order-of-operations errors, misinterpreting vendor- or OS-specific syntax, and suggesting untrusted package sources (supply-chain risk). Agentic setups with shell or API access expand the blast radius to environment-wide compromise via prompt-injection, credential exfiltration, and unintended command execution. Oversight risk is significant: authoritative-seeming, vendor-specific configs can induce deference and reduce independent verification, so subtle ACL/NAT/order-of-operations or interface-binding bugs may slip through and be discovered only under attack or during failover. Cross-vendor syntax drift (e.g., iptables vs nftables, ASA/FTD vs Palo Alto, Windows Defender Firewall vs pfSense, or cloud security groups) increases mismatch risk. Using third-party LLMs may also leak network diagrams, IP ranges, logs, or credentials if redaction and compliant processing are not enforced.

gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward if experts retain authority over technical correctness and security: rapid first drafts and revisions tailored to different audiences; enforce style/consistency; generate step-by-step/checklists, troubleshooting trees, and FAQs; synthesize from vendor docs and tickets into KB articles; translate and simplify; de-duplicate and refactor legacy manuals. With mandated test runs and peer security review, typical savings are about 30–60% of authoring time (e.g., 2–8 hours saved on a 5–15 hour document), roughly $100–$800 per manual at $50–$100/hr, while maintaining quality.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Security, Privacy, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical: Yes (organizational availability, integrity, and confidentiality can be impacted by bad instructions). Compared with human-only drafting, LLM+expert workflows introduce moderate incremental risk: fluent but incorrect or outdated steps (e.g., disabling firewalls, weak cipher suites, bypassing cert validation) can slip in; polished language and seemingly authoritative rationales increase deference and reduce independent testing (capability-induced oversight risk); inclusion or inference of sensitive details (IPs, hostnames, credentials, tickets with PII) can leak through the model or end up embedded in public-facing docs; prompt-injection from untrusted source text pasted into the LLM can steer docs toward insecure practices; attackers may seed public pages the LLM consults or exploit agent tooling. Many errors are catchable via peer review and lab testing, but subtle security regressions and environment-specific misconfigurations can be missed under time pressure.

Title: Computer Network Support Specialists
Task: Run monthly network reports.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: LLMs can consolidate outputs from multiple monitoring tools, draft executive summaries for different audiences, highlight trends/anomalies, generate tables/graphs, and create follow-up questions—reducing manual synthesis work. With deterministic data pulls and expert spot-checks to keep quality, typical savings are 30–120 minutes per cycle (approximately $30–$200 at $30–$100/hr), larger in multi-tool or multi-tenant environments. Savings are realized when the model works from frozen, audited exports/APIs, cites each figure with the underlying query and time range, and all numerics are validated by lightweight scripts or dashboard spot-checks—maintaining human-equivalent quality.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Privacy, Security, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: The task affects organizational reliability and compliance: monthly uptime/capacity/SLA/security summaries feed budgeting, audits, and customer reports. LLMs can mis-aggregate metrics (time windows, units, deduplication), hallucinate explanations, omit rare-but-important incidents, or overstate availability; fluent prose can trigger automation bias, reducing independent spot-checks. Handling logs/netflow/tickets through third-party LLMs risks exposure of IPs, user identifiers, and potentially PHI/credentials; agentic setups may face prompt-injection from log content, over-broad tool permissions, or data exfiltration. Attackers could also abuse an LLM interface to generate convincing but falsified reports or pivot queries across systems. Many issues are catchable if experts verify figures against authoritative dashboards and require traceable, reproducible queries with citations, but subtle omissions or aggregation errors can slip through in long reports.

Title: Computer User Support Specialists
Task: Oversee the daily performance of computer systems.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: As a read-only copilot, LLMs can condense noisy logs, correlate alerts, surface anomalies, generate NL-to-query for monitoring tools, draft daily health reports, propose runbooks, and pre-fill tickets/status updates. With humans verifying high-severity findings against source dashboards and keeping changes/manual actions human-approved, teams often save 30–120 minutes per specialist per day (≈$20–$160/day at $40–$80 /hr), reduce MTTR by 10–30% on well-instrumented services, and cut report/ticket prep time by 50–80%. Rewards are highest when tightly integrated with observability tools, runbooks, and strict human verification of high-severity items, maintaining parity with human-only quality.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Privacy, Security, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: This task is safety critical: missed or mishandled performance issues can lead to outages, data loss, SLA penalties, and security incidents. LLM use adds risk via plausible but incorrect or incomplete log/event summaries, false negatives, and invented explanations; capability-induced oversight risk (automation bias) can make operators rely on summaries and check dashboards less thoroughly; privacy risk from exposing PII, credentials, or proprietary data embedded in logs/metrics; security risk from prompt injection and tool misuse if agents read untrusted telemetry or can execute actions; adversaries can craft logs, alerts, or emails to induce the model to suppress or misprioritize alerts or to run unsafe commands. Many failures are hard to detect quickly because omissions in summaries are subtle and only surface post-incident. Relative to human-only workflows, LLM+human moderately increases the chance of missed/delayed incidents (≈1.2–1.6x without strong guardrails) and materially increases privacy/security exposure if data leaves controlled boundaries or if agents can act autonomously.

Title: Computer User Support Specialists
Task: Set up equipment for employee use, performing or ensuring proper installation of cables, operating systems, or appropriate software.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward when used for planning and documentation, not autonomous execution: generate tailored checklists and step-by-step playbooks per OS/role, draft scripts/configs with dry-run guards and rollback notes, inventory drivers and package manifests, propose GPO/MDM profiles with version-pinned references, auto-generate tickets/change logs/user comms, and summarize vendor KBs. With expert review, sandbox testing, and approval gates, teams can cut routine setups by ~20–40% (10–30 minutes per device; ~$5–$30 at $30–$60/hr) and complex rollouts by ~0.5–2 hours while maintaining quality.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical: endpoint setup affects security posture, data availability, and business continuity. LLMs can produce plausible but incorrect commands or policies (e.g., disabling disk encryption, misconfiguring firewall/MDM/GPO, wrong drivers), reference unsafe sources, or hallucinate flags—issues that may not surface until later incidents. If connected to RMM/MDM or shell tools, prompt/command injection and supply-chain risks can cause rapid, wide-scale misconfiguration or malware installation. Chatting about device setup can leak credentials, serials, network details, or license keys. Because frontier LLM outputs look authoritative, technicians may copy–paste without full vendor-doc verification, increasing oversight risk versus human-only SOPs. Compared with expert-only workflows, LLM+human raises both error likelihood and blast radius unless strong controls (sandbox testing, source pinning, approval gates) are enforced.

Title: Computer User Support Specialists
Task: Read technical manuals, confer with users, or conduct computer diagnostics to investigate and resolve problems or to provide technical assistance and support.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward when used for retrieval, drafting, and summarization rather than autonomous action: normalize/parse logs, cross-reference manuals/KBs, propose step-by-step playbooks, generate and comment scripts, summarize tickets, create user-friendly, multilingual responses, and speed triage/routing. With human verification (e.g., check against vendor docs or run scripts in a sandbox), teams typically save 5–12 minutes on a 20–30 minute L1 ticket and 0.5–2 hours on complex L2 cases (about $5–$150 at $30–$75/hr), while maintaining expert quality; added safety checks cost ~1–3 minutes but preserve net savings.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Misinformation, Privacy, Malicious actors and Misuse, Toxicity, Discrimination
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical: incorrect or insecure troubleshooting steps can wipe data, expose credentials, disable protections, or misconfigure production systems, causing outages, compliance violations, or breaches. Using LLMs increases risk vs. human-only support because (a) plausible but wrong commands/registry edits/config flags are easy to copy-paste under time pressure (capability-induced oversight); (b) models may suggest disabling security controls to “fix” issues; (c) prompt-injection via pasted logs/URLs or compromised KBs can elicit unsafe instructions or secret leakage; (d) tickets/logs may contain PII/credentials, creating privacy and data residency risk; (e) attackers can probe LLM-assisted chat to extract runbooks or craft targeted phishing; (f) biased/toxic phrasing can harm users or create HR risk. Mitigations (trace every step to vendor docs, sandbox/test commands, enforce read-only defaults, redact/anonymize data, audit logs, role-based tools) reduce but don’t eliminate risk—subtle errors and oversights can still evade detection in complex environments.

Title: Computer User Support Specialists

For complex incidents, savings are moderate (~10–20%) due to necessary expert verification. gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Privacy, Security, Malicious actors and Misuse, Toxicity, Discrimination
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical: incorrect troubleshooting guidance can cause data loss, downtime, or security exposure; support tasks often involve password resets, permission changes, device wipes, registry edits, and handling sensitive logs or screen captures. LLMs increase risk by producing confident but wrong steps (e.g., disabling EDR/AV, unsafe shell or registry commands), omitting critical prechecks, or hallucinating fixes; capability-induced oversight means agents’ fluent reasoning can cause technicians to defer and skip sandboxing or change-control reviews. Agentic setups are vulnerable to prompt-injection via logs, error messages, or linked web content, tool misuse, and data exfiltration. Privacy risk arises if PII, credentials, or configuration data are ingested or retained. Attackers can socially engineer LLM-driven triage to reveal information or approve resets. Toxic or biased language can harm user experience and create compliance risk. Compared to human-only workflows, using LLMs without strict controls likely increases the probability of a harmful action per resolved ticket by ~1.5x–3x; with SOP gating, least-privilege tools, identity verification, sandbox testing, and audit trails, residual risk can approach human-only levels but remains nonzero due to automation bias and injection risks.

Title: Computer User Support Specialists
Task: Install and perform minor repairs to hardware, software, or peripheral equipment, following design or installation specifications.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: LLMs can materially reduce time on routine installs and minor repairs by generating tailored checklists, mapping vendor specs to the exact OS/hardware, drafting validated command sequences (with comments/dry-runs), summarizing logs/error codes, and drafting tickets/user comms. With experts verifying against vendor docs and testing in a sandbox, typical cycle-time savings are about 15–30% per incident (e.g., 5–20 minutes on 30–90 minute tasks, ≈$5–$40 at $20–$120/hr). For repeatable fleet tasks, script/template generation plus documentation can save 10–30% of effort while maintaining quality if scripts undergo peer review and staged rollout.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical: yes. Installing or repairing hardware/software often requires privileged access; wrong commands, registry edits, driver/firmware choices, or security settings can cause data loss, device bricking, outages, or open attack surface. LLMs increase risk via (a) convincing but incorrect or incomplete troubleshooting steps; (b) hallucinated commands/paths, unsafe registry edits, or suggesting downloads from untrusted sources; (c) security misconfigurations (e.g., disabling protections to ‘fix’ issues); (d) privacy leakage if endpoint logs/PII are pasted into non-compliant models; (e) prompt injection or tool misuse in agentic setups driving destructive actions at scale via RMM/PSA tools. Capability-induced oversight risk: fluent, step-by-step outputs can induce deference, reducing independent checks (e.g., running write/delete commands without dry-runs), especially under time pressure or with junior staff. Compared to human-only support, naive LLM+human use can raise the probability of a harmful action by roughly 1.5–3x on complex incidents; with guardrails (enterprise model, read-only reconnaissance first, verified vendor sources, sandbox testing, change approvals), residual risk increase can be limited to marginal levels (<10%) but not eliminated.

Title: Computer User Support Specialists

gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward when used as an assistant, not the decision-maker: draft stakeholder questionnaires and agendas; synthesize interview notes; cluster themes; generate user stories and acceptance criteria; surface conflicts and missing NFRs via checklists; draft traceability matrices; translate between business and technical language or across languages. gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Privacy, Security, Malicious actors and Misuse, Discrimination
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical at the organizational level: flawed or incomplete requirements can produce outages, costly rework, security/compliance gaps, and data exposure. LLMs raise risk by generating persuasive but incorrect or incomplete requirement documents (hallucinated constraints, omission of non-functional requirements such as security, privacy, accessibility, performance, and disaster recovery), drifting into premature solution designs, and weak traceability to stakeholder inputs. Capability-induced oversight risk is material: polished BRDs/PRDs can induce stakeholders to defer and sign off with less scrutiny. Privacy/Security risks arise if stakeholder PII, credentials, or architecture details are shared with non-compliant tools; prompt-injection from pasted logs/tickets or adversarial stakeholders can steer outputs; agentic tools may leak or modify documents. Misuse: malicious insiders could shape prompts to embed excessive privileges or backdoors; external actors can leverage convincing AI-authored communications. Bias risk: under-specifying accessibility or multilingual needs and stereotyping user personas. Many issues are catchable with structured reviews, traceability, and security/privacy gates, hence risk 3.

Title: Computer User Support Specialists
Task: Enter commands and observe system functioning to verify correct operations and detect errors.

Typical savings 5–20 minutes on routine tickets and 15–45 minutes on complex triage (about $3–$35 at $25–$50/hr) while maintaining human quality if commands are reviewed, run in read-only/sandbox first, and facts are verified against trusted docs.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical: incorrect or destructive commands and misdiagnosed system states can cause outages, data loss, security exposure, or SLA penalties. LLMs increase risk via (a) plausible but dangerous or OS-inappropriate commands, misused flags, or hallucinated tooling; (b) overconfident log/metric interpretations that are hard to catch amidst noisy telemetry, combined with automation bias (humans defer to fluent explanations); (c) tool-use vulnerabilities—prompt/command injection from logs, shell/CLI injection, and unintended privilege escalation if agents can execute commands; (d) privacy/security leakage when pasting logs or configs containing credentials/PII to external services. Compared to human-only workflows, the L LM+human pairing expands the attack surface (prompt/log injection, tool or API misuse) and raises capability-induced oversight risk—operators may skip man-page checks or dry-runs because the model’s explanation sounds authoritative. Many damaging failures (e.g., rm/recursive flags, mis-scoped kubectl, misapplied SQL in prod, or misreading a transient alarm) are subtle and only evident post-execution, making them hard to detect reliably before harm occurs.

Title: Computer User Support Specialists
Task: Maintain records of daily data communication transactions, problems and remedial actions taken, or installation activities.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward for drafting and structuring rather than truth-judgment: auto-summarize chats and console output into standardized fields, extract entities and timestamps, normalize categories, link KB/runbooks, and flag missing data. Typical savings of ~1–5 minutes per ticket or install record (≈20–50 /hr), roughly $0.30–$4 per record, plus faster handoffs and audit readiness. Gains shrink on complex incidents where verification dominates but remain positive when the model pre-fills structured fields and links to sources.
gpt5_risks_types: Privacy, Security, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse, Discrimination
gpt5_risks_justifications: Organizationally safety-critical: inaccurate or incomplete records can impede incident response, audits, and compliance, and can obscure security issues. LLMs increase risk by producing persuasive but incorrect or incomplete summaries (e.g., wrong timestamps, systems, versions, IPs; missing escalation steps), fabricating details, or misclassifying events; capability-induced oversight risk means staff may defer to fluent notes and review less rigorously. Records often include PII, credentials, or network topology—raising privacy and security exposure if models are not isolated; prompt injection from pasted logs can corrupt outputs; agentic setups can overwrite tickets; adversaries could seed misleading content to alter the record. Relative to human-only workflows, LLM+human can raise the chance that material documentation errors persist by ~1.3x–2x under light oversight; with strict provenance (source excerpts and timestamps), DLP/redaction, access controls, and mandatory human sign-off, residual risk approaches parity.

Title: Computer User Support Specialists
Task: Refer major hardware or software problems or defective products to vendors or technicians for service.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward when used for drafting and routing rather than deciding: auto-extract error codes, compile minimal reproducible steps and affected assets, summarize logs, map to KB articles, pre-fill vendor/RMA forms, and generate clear escalation notes and attachments. With human verification and whitelisted contacts, typical savings are 10–30 minutes per major referral (often 20–50% of the referral effort), i.e., roughly $5–$25 per case at $30–$ 60/hr), plus reduced back-and-forth with vendors and shorter MTTR; larger gains in high-volume environments.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Privacy, Security, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical in many environments: incorrect or delayed escalation can lead to extended outages, data loss, missed security incidents, or regulatory impact; in critical infrastructure/healthcare, downstream effects can affect safety. LLM-specific risks: (1) Misinformation—plausible but wrong triage (e.g., misclassifying severity, hallucinating vendor contacts/RMA policies, misrouting to the wrong vendor), which can delay fixes; (2) Privacy—logs/screenshots often contain credentials, PII, or confidential configs; sharing with a non-compliant model or including them in vendor tickets can leak sensitive data; (3) Security—prompt injection in error logs or tickets, supply-chain phishing (LLM proposes or trusts spoofed ‘vendor’ portals), tool/agent misuse if auto-filling web forms; (4) Malicious misuse—attackers can craft errors that induce oversharing or escalation to attacker-controlled ‘support’. Capability-induced oversight risk: fluent, authoritative LLM summaries may reduce human scrutiny, increasing under‑escalation or acceptance of fabricated details. Relative to human-only triage, unmitigated LLM assistance can moderately increase risk (≈1.5–2× likelihood of misrouting or under‑escalation) due to automation bias and fabricated details; with safeguards (SOP checklists, whitelist of vendor contacts/portals, mandatory log redaction, and documented human sign‑off), residual risk approaches parity (≈≤1.1×).

Title: Computer User Support Specialists
Task: Prepare evaluations of software or hardware, and recommend improvements or upgrades.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward if constrained to synthesis and drafting, with humans validating facts and running pilots. LLMs can: rapidly assemble feature/compatibility matrices from vendor docs, generate evaluation criteria, draft TCO comparisons and procurement justifications, outline migration/rollback plans, produce user comms and change notes, and propose test plans or scripts (reviewed). Typical savings: approximately 2–10 hours per evaluation (of roughly 6–30 hours total) via faster literature/vendor triage and report drafting—about 20–50% time reduction when quality is held constant through human verification—equating to roughly $150–$1,000 at $75–$100/hr. Gains shrink for complex environments where validation dominates.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Privacy, Security, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical: Yes. Faulty recommendations on software/hardware can trigger outages, data loss, security exposure, license noncompliance, or major cost overruns. LLM-specific risks: (1) Misinformation—confident but wrong claims about compatibility, performance, end-of-life/support status, licensing terms, or TCO/ROI; subtle omissions or hallucinated benchmarks are hard to spot and can sway decisions. (2) Security—suggesting unpatched or end-of-life products, unsafe config changes, or unvetted downloads; agentic browsing can be prompt-injected by vendor pages/fora; toolchain vulnerabilities could leak credentials or artifacts; auto-generated upgrade scripts may be destructive if not sandboxed. (3) Privacy—uploading device inventories, logs, or contracts with PII/secret infrastructure details to noncompliant models risks exposure. (4) Malicious misuse—attackers/vendors can seed persuasive content that LLMs summarize, or craft injection-laced docs to bias outcomes. Many errors are catchable with structured verification (vendor docs/HCLs, pilot testing, security review, change control), but under time pressure or when models appear highly competent, some failures may escape, hence risk = 3.

LLMs raise risk by (a) misinformation: hallucinated or omitted events, incorrect timestamps, ordering, or fields; subtle summarization errors are hard to spot and may break ingestion/parsing or create gaps that persist to audits; (b) capability‑induced oversight: fluent, well‑structured summaries increase deference, so admins review fewer raw entries, raising the chance that critical omissions go undetected; (c) privacy: logs often contain credentials, keys, IPs, device identifiers, and user/PHI; sending them to external models risks data leakage or model retention ; (d) security: prompt-injection via log contents (e.g., attacker-controlled user agents or payloads) can cause tool-using agents to exfiltrate or delete data; granting agents write access to log stores/CMDBs risks corruption, chain-of-custody loss, or evidence spoliation; model/toolchain vulnerabilities expand the attack surface; (e) misuse: insiders or attackers could leverage the model to rapidly enumerate sensitive infrastructure details or craft tailored exploits. Overall, compared to human-only workflows, capable LLMs increase oversight risk because outputs appear authoritative and time pressure can discourage full raw-log verification.

Title: Network and Computer Systems Administrators

With strict guardrails (PII redaction, approved on‑prem or compliant models, evidence‑linked outputs, mandatory independent numeric checks and threat modeling), teams can typically reduce discovery/documentation effort by ~20–40% on a 100–200‑hour planning phase (≈20–80 hours; ≈$2k–$10k at $100–$250/hr) while maintaining expert‑level quality; added verification steps (≈2–6 hours) still net a substantial time/cost gain.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety‑critical: flawed requirement gathering or forecasting can yield outages, security gaps, compliance failures, or costly over/under‑provisioning at the organizational level. LLMs raise risk by (a) confident but wrong summaries or extrapolations (missing edge constraints, misreading SLAs, optimistic capacity estimates), (b) capability‑induced oversight risk—authoritative narratives cause admins to defer and skip independent sizing/validation, (c) security/privacy exposure of network diagrams, configs, tickets, or customer PII to third‑party models, and (d) new attack surface: prompt injection via pasted logs/URLs, data exfiltration through tools/RAG, and model‑assisted social engineering. Compared to human‑only workflows, introducing an LLM without strong controls plausibly increases the probability that a requirements defect or leakage goes undetected by ~1.5–3x, especially in complex, multi‑stakeholder environments; even with reviews, rare but high‑impact errors (e.g., missed compliance constraint) are harder to spot when hidden in convincing summaries.

Title: Network and Computer Systems Administrators

With admins verifying numbers/terms and finance/procurement retaining sign-off, typical savings are 1–4 hours per routine purchase and 5–10 hours for multi-vendor or renewal cycles (about $75–$800 at $50–$80/hr), plus 1–3 days faster cycle time from quicker correspondence and document triage. Using enterprise-grade deployments (data controls, logging) and standard verification templates keeps mitigation costs low relative to time saved.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse, Discrimination
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical at the organizational level: procurement mistakes or manipulation can cause material financial loss, contractual exposure, operational downtime, or data leakage. Using LLMs increases risk versus human-only workflows mainly via: (1) capability-induced oversight—convincing quote comparisons or contract summaries can lead admins to defer and miss subtle terms (auto-renewals, support tiers, data-processing, SLAs, termination fees), SKU mismatches, or recurring vs one-time costs; (2) security/privacy—sharing vendor quotes, banking details, or network specs with non-enterprise models can leak sensitive data; agentic tools that browse or parse vendor PDFs/websites are vulnerable to prompt injection or data exfiltration; (3) misuse/BEC—LLM-assisted email agents can be socially engineered to route POs or accept fraudulent bank-account changes; (4) misinformation—hallucinated part numbers, misread quantities/taxes/freight, or incorrect TCO rollups can lead to bad purchases; (5) discrimination—if the model suggests or filters vendors, it may reflect biased training data. Many errors are catchable with disciplined verification, two-person approvals, and finance/legal review, but subtle contractual or payment details and injection-driven behaviors can escape detection in fast-paced workflows, so risk is moderate and higher than human-only baselines.

Title: Network and Computer Systems Administrators
Task: Implement and provide technical support for voice services and equipment, such as private branch exchange, voice mail system, and telecom system.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward when LLMs act as accelerators, not authorities: summarize vendor docs and TAC threads; draft dial plans, translation rules, COR/COS matrices, and test plans; generate CLI/SIPp test scripts; parse logs/pcaps/SIP traces and produce timelines; map features across platforms (e.g., CUCM↔Asterisk) for migrations; draft user comms, runbooks, and KBs. Typical savings while maintaining quality with expert verification: implementation projects 15–30% (approximately 3–12 hours on a 20–40 hour build, roughly $300–$1,800 at $100–$150/hr); incident triage/MTTR reduction 10–30 minutes per ticket (approximately $17–$75); documentation and change paperwork 30–60% drafting-time reduction. These gains hold if changes remain gated by lab/staging tests, peer review, and E911/security checklists.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: The task is safety-critical: misconfiguration of PBX/VoIP/telecom systems can cut off business voice services, break E911 location/call routing, expose voicemail or recordings, and enable toll fraud—causing operational, financial, and potential life-safety harm. LLMs increase risk by: generating plausible but incorrect vendor-specific configs/CLI (e.g., dial plans, SIP trunk settings, NAT/firewall rules, TLS/SRTP, certificates) that can silently degrade quality or disable emergency calling; omitting mandatory checks (COS/COR, caller ID masking, failover routes, rate limits); recommending insecure defaults (open SIP/RTSP ports, weak auth, disabled encryption); hallucinating feature availability or syntax across platforms (CUCM/IOS/Asterisk/Avaya/Mitel) leading to outages during change windows; and capability-induced oversight—admins may defer to detailed LLM runbooks and perform less exhaustive peer review. Agentic use with device or API access amplifies blast radius, and pasting logs/configs into non-compliant tools risks leakage of CDRs, phone numbers, voicemail content, or credentials; prompt injection via untrusted logs/KBs can steer tools to unsafe actions. These failures can be difficult to detect in advance—intermittent QoS/codec/NAT issues, E911 misrouting that only appears under specific locations/failover, or exposed SIP services exploited for rapid toll fraud. Because outputs look vendor-credible, admins may truncate lab validation or peer review (capability-induced oversight). Compared to human-only workflows, end-to-end risk can rise roughly 1.5–3x if LLMs generate or apply configs without strict checklists, lab tests, and change control; risk approaches parity when models are kept read-only, outputs are traced to vendor docs, and mandatory E911/security validations are enforced.

Title: Network and Computer Systems Administrators

With human verification against the SKU master and procurement rules, typical savings are about 20–40% of admin effort on inventory cycles (e.g., 1–3 hours per month, roughly $50–$300 at $50–$100/hr) while maintaining quality; larger gains from agentic integrations exist but raise risk, so a recommend-only posture offers a good balance.

Compared with human-only workflows, LLM+human moderately increases risk (often 10–30%) because some failures are only discovered during emergencies; strong controls (read-only suggestions, SKU master validation, segregation of duties, approvals, DLP and prompt-injection hardening) keep most errors catchable.

Tool-using/browsing agents can be prompt-injected by web docs or vendor sites, leading to data exfiltration or biased recommendations; code-generation can pull unsafe libraries; and pasting network diagrams, logs, or configs into non-compliant models risks sensitive-data leakage. gpt5_rewards_justifications: High rewards when used as a paired assistant for boilerplate, scaffolding, refactoring, test generation, API usage examples, code translation, documentation, and review summaries. Communication and ops tasks (writing PR descriptions, runbook drafts) also accelerate. Quality can be maintained if critical logic, security-sensitive code, and infra changes receive heightened review and all LLM-produced code is treated as untrusted input, fully covered by tests, and security-reviewed; run LLMs in access-controlled, privacy-preserving environments to prevent IP/secret leakage.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse, Discrimination
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical at organizational/societal scale: defects and insecure code can trigger outages, data loss, breaches, or downstream exploitation, supply-chain compromise, and regulatory exposure. Additional vectors: prompt injection via README/comments or issue text that steers coding agents; dependency hallucination and typosquatting; license contamination; leakage of secrets or proprietary code via prompts or logs; agents executing destructive shell commands; biased or toxic outputs baked into user-facing strings. Many errors are only caught with rigorous CI/CD, tests, SAST/DAST, code review by senior engineers, and security triage; without that, harmful defects can reach production.

gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Often safety-critical at the organizational level: an incorrect or insecure fix can trigger outages, data loss, or breaches. Relative to human-only workflows, risk rises moderately because convincing patches and green tests can reduce scrutiny; mitigate with mandatory code review, pair debugging, reproducible repro steps, property-based and fuzz tests, SAST/DAST, secret scanning, dependency pinning, and staged rollouts with monitoring.
